bull.b: Atlassian’s subscription-led model creates recurring revenue and opportunities to expand users, products and plan tiers within existing accounts. Its marketplace, integrations and developer ecosystem can increase product stickiness, support adoption and reinforce the platform’s role in customers’ workflows over time.

Strong cloud growth, rising contracted backlog and NRR above 120% indicate that customers are expanding usage rather than merely renewing. Growth in large-account cohorts further supports durable enterprise penetration, cross-sell potential and a broader revenue base over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and gross margins
bull.b: Robust operating and free cash flow demonstrate effective conversion of revenue into cash despite reported accounting losses. Combined with approximately 85% gross margins, this gives Atlassian meaningful capacity to fund product investment, AI development and customer expansion while supporting financial resilience.

bear.b: Persistent net losses and volatile operating profitability show that strong software gross margins have not yet translated consistently into durable earnings. Renewed negative EBITDA margin suggests continuing cost pressure, leaving future profit conversion dependent on disciplined spending and sustained revenue growth.

bear.t: Moderating FY27 growth and margin outlook
bear.b: The lower ARR outlook implies that growth may decelerate from the recent pace as Atlassian laps acquisition benefits and manages uncertainty. Full-year margin guidance well below Q4’s 12% also indicates that investment and planning assumptions could weigh on earnings quality over the coming year.

Although leverage has improved materially, debt remains sizable relative to equity and increases claims on future cash generation. Combined with negative returns on equity, this limits balance-sheet flexibility and could constrain capital allocation if profitability or cash conversion weakens during the forecast period.
